Subject: Data handling questions for EU pin + temporary operator access

Hi Ben —

Quick follow up from our security review: before we proceed with the DPA redlines, two operational clarifications would help us sign: 

1) Pseudonymization: Can Redwood apply an irreversible pseudonymization step (or support customer-supplied irreversible tokenization) before any data leaves the EU region? We need to avoid reversible transformations for identity fields unless explicitly requested.

2) Operator/KMS access during temporary failover: we understand you offer short ephemeral cross-region windows for failover. For audit reasons we need explicit commitments on whether Redwood operators (or subprocessor staff) ever have access to cleartext during those windows, and if so how long.

Attached are our DPA redlines for context. If you can summarize what you can commit to (e.g., EU pin with a 48–72h transient exception and operator access model) that will speed internal approval.

Attachment: bluepeak-dpa-redlines.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Sam

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tanaka <sam.tanaka@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data handling questions for EU pin + temporary operator access

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear notes and the redlines. Short answers up front, then detail and next steps below: 

- Pseudonymization: We can support a pseudonymization workflow. By default our platform performs configurable field-level hashing and deterministic tokenization; however, we cannot claim irreversible cryptographic destruction unless the customer supplies the keys and you accept the downstream limitations (e.g., no rollbacks). We can document an irreversible pipeline if BluePeak supplies a customer-managed key (CMK) and requires that we never persist the cleartext.

- Operator/KMS access during transient failover: Our standard model is region affinity (EU-hosted), with a short transient failover window. We do not provide operators with access to unencrypted model inputs/outputs as part of routine failover. If a customer requests operator-assisted troubleshooting that requires decryption, that requires an explicit escalation and is logged; access can be granted under strict controls and timebox (we typically propose 48–72 hours max, with customer approval and an audit trail).

Proposed compromise for BluePeak to consider:
- Commit to EU region affinity for routine processing.
- Allow a documented transient cross-region hop (72h default) for availability, but make it explicit in the DPA and require customer consent for each activation.
- Offer two pseudonymization options: (A) Redwood-managed deterministic tokenization (reversible to us for debugging) or (B) customer-managed irreversible pseudonymization using your CMK (irreversible to Redwood).

Would BluePeak accept a 72h default window with the option to shorten to 48h by contract? If so, legal can accept our template DPA language and we can provide a DocuSign link for the addendum.

I've cc'd Marissa and Neha to align on legal/ops mechanics and to draft the DPA snippet.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the quick turn. BluePeak is comfortable with the approach in principle. A couple of small asks before we route to procurement: 

- Can the default transient window be set to 48 hours in the addendum? We prefer the shorter window as the base contract option.
- For the CMK irreversible path, our legal will want a short paragraph stating that Redwood has "no ability to recover" pseudonymized identifiers if customer destroys keys. We understand the operational tradeoffs.

If you can update the addendum to reflect a 48h default (instead of 72h) and include the CMK irreversibility language, we can circulate internally and sign. Please send the DocuSign link when ready — legal@bluepeakhealth.com will review.
